title: Mutable Prompt Template Binding — prototype notes
content:
Context and motivation:
This is a personal prototype notes doc for a client-side / session-aware mechanism that lets applications bind mutable values into prompt templates without re-sending or re-compiling the template each call. Goal is to reduce token waste, enable client-level personalization, and allow safe, auditable diffs for rollout and A/B testing. This is intentionally lightweight and experimental — focuses on the API shape, storage/serialization format, and runtime behavior.

User stories / examples:
- Chat app: user sets a dynamic system-template variables (name, timezone, preferred tone). The client binds the variables once at session start; subsequent calls only send variable deltas when they change.
- Multi-tenant app: each tenant has a base template. The app attaches tenant-scoped overrides locally and only shares binding IDs with server endpoints.
- Canary rollouts: Devs want to hot-swap a single variable across 10% of sessions without changing the template.

Key constraints and requirements:
- Minimal per-call token overhead for stable templates.
- Bindings must be versioned and content-addressable for cache keys and audit.
- Server (hosted inference) must be able to reconstruct full prompt deterministically given: template-id, binding-id/revision, and optional inline deltas.
- Client-side should support offline/resume semantics: serialize bindings to local store, rehydrate on reconnect.
- Privacy: binding storage on hosted plane should be optional; clients may prefer ephemeral-only binding IDs that are resolved by client-side expansion.

High-level design (two modes):
1) Server-resolved bindings (default): client sends template-id + binding-id. Server fetches binding content from customer namespace (or from client provided signed blob). Good when central auditing/quality checks are required.
2) Client-resolved bindings (privacy/edge mode): client sends template-id + binding-hash + inline compressed patch. Server verifies hash and applies patch during render. Server does not store binding contents after request.

API shapes (sketch):
- POST /v1/generate
  body: {
    "model": "rdx-2-small",
    "template_id": "tpl:welcome/v2",
    "binding": {
      "mode": "id" | "inline",
      "id": "bind:usr-12/20241115/3",        # content-addressable id or session id
      "rev": "3",                           # optional revision number
      "inline_patch": "base64gzip(...)",    # required for mode=inline or to include deltas
      "meta": {"client_tz": "America/NYC"} # optional small KV with non-sensitive metadata
    },
    "input": {"user_message": "..."},
    "options": {"stream": true, "max_tokens": 400}
  }

- Binding management (client SDK)
  POST /v1/bindings  -> creates server-side binding, returns id, revision, and ca-hash
  GET  /v1/bindings/{id}  -> returns metadata and signed manifest (if permitted)
  PUT  /v1/bindings/{id}  -> create new revision (server-side stored)
  DELETE /v1/bindings/{id} -> soft-delete (audit trails retained)

Serialization format (local):
- Compact JSON manifest with CA-hash and small diffs encoded as ndjson of ops. Example manifest below (this is meant to be small and easy to persist):

{"ca_hash": "sha256:abcd...", "template_id": "tpl:welcome/v2", "rev": "3", "ops": ["replace path=/vars/user_name value=Jorge", "rm path=/vars/email_pref"], "created": "2024-11-15T14:22:00Z"}

We keep ops small (text ops) to avoid re-sending full template. For large changes, client should send a full inline patch (gzip+base64) and server will store a new binding revision if requested.

Cache key considerations:
- Cache key = model + template_id + binding_ca_hash + options(max_len, top_p, etc).
- If client uses inline patches but provides ca_hash, the server MUST verify patch -> hash before using the cache.

Interplay with KV / prefix caching on serving runtime:
- Runtime has two-tier cache: 1) template compile artifacts (tokenization, special tokens, structured output hints). 2) prefix/KV cache per active session.
- Binding changes should invalidate prefix cache only for the sessions affected. Where possible, we avoid invalidating compiled artifacts.

Security and privacy notes:
- Sensitive fields in bindings (PII, PII-like preferences) must be flagged in manifest (field-level sensitivity) and encrypted at rest when stored server-side.
- For client-resolved mode, signing keys and short-lived signatures are needed to allow server verify-only without permanent storage. Consider using signed binding manifests (JWT with CA-hash).

Edge cases and open questions (TODOs):
- How to handle functions/tool-calling when the template binds function names? If binding changes function signature, runtime must fallback to safe mode.
- How granular should ops be? Text diff vs structured path ops. Opinion: structured path ops helpful for guards but harder for free-form templating.
- Garbage collection for bindings: rev retention policies by age + last-used. Integrate with billing reports.
- Multi-client merge conflicts: if two clients update same binding id, must create separate revisions and track parent pointers.

Prototype client SDK pseudo-code (JS):
const binding = await sdk.bindings.create({templateId: 'tpl:welcome/v2', ops: [{op:'replace', path:'/vars/name', value:'Ethan'}]});
const resp = await sdk.generate({model:'rdx-2', templateId: 'tpl:welcome/v2', binding:{mode:'id', id:binding.id}});

Server-side render flow (sketch):
1) Authenticate request, validate template_id.
2) Resolve binding: if mode=="id" -> load binding manifest from store; if mode=="inline" -> verify ca_hash and apply patch to template in memory.
3) Validate binding against template schema (if template has a contract).
4) Render final prompt. Compute cache key, try prefix/KV cache, execute model.
5) Emit telemetry: binding.id OR binding.ca_hash, ops_count, render_time, cache_hit

ASCII diagram (simplified):
Client SDK ----> Redwood API Gateway ---> Binding Store (optional)
       |                 |
       |-- inline patch ->|
       |                 v
       |            Rendering Layer ---> Serving runtime -> Model

Notes on audits and explainability:
- Store minimal diff metadata in audit log (op counts, field names changed, binding id, rev). Avoid logging actual sensitive values unless flagged and encrypted.
- Provide an endpoint for "dry-run render" that returns the final prompt (with masking) for debugging in dev environment only.

Acceptance tests / quick validation plan:
- Unit: verify ca_hash computed from inline patch matches expected for many permutations.
- Integration: create binding, send generate with id, confirm server reconstructs same prompt as inline mode.
- Perf: measure token overhead for binding-by-id vs sending full template across a 10k-session workload.
- Privacy test: ensure client-resolved mode leaves no residual binding in server store when mode="inline" and retention=ephemeral.

Follow-ups and next steps:
- Spike: implement minimal server verification layer (inline patch -> ca_hash check) in dev cluster. Target: low-effort PoC in 1 week.
- UX: add small SDK helper to diff current binding vs last-sent binding to compute ops automatically.
- Product: propose retention defaults and opt-in enterprise options for server-side binding storage.

Brain dump / miscellaneous thoughts (notes to self):
- Might be useful to treat bindings as "small templates" with templating language restricted to KV insertion only (no control flow) to simplify verification.
- Consider protobuf compact binary manifest for local store to save bytes in highly-constrained mobile apps.
- Evaluate interplay with Redwood Optimize: quantization or batching decisions could vary per-binding if bound variables change expected output length distribution.

Unresolved decisions for future doc:
- binding_id naming scheme: content-addressed (sha256) vs opaque session-scoped ids. Tradeoffs: CA => deterministic caches; opaque => easier multi-revision management for UIs.
- schema enforcement: should templates declare strict types for variables? If yes, provide typed manifest and stricter server validation.

End of prototype notes.

Quick references and pickups:
- Implementation spike branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/432
- Related ticket: PROJ-1192 (binding lifecycle and GC)
- Slack thread: #dev-dx 'mutable-binding' (search Nov 2024)
